Anna (CS): FYI CopperGate is scheduled to rotate their KMS key next week. They asked about impacts to Redwood Private (VPC) - need to confirm audit/logging and cross-account IAM details. renewal risk if rotation breaks ingest :grimacing:

Raj (Solutions): Thanks. Do we know if they're using AWS KMS or an HSM-backed customer key? or using our managed key?

Anna (CS): They said customer-managed AWS KMS CMK in their account, not using our managed key. They also want audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance.

Maria (NetEng): For Private deployment the important bits are: VPC endpoints for S3/CloudTrail, route for outbound to KMS endpoints (or use VPC endpoint for KMS), and ensuring the S3 bucket for audit logs is in the allowed list. If they're rotating, the key policy must allow Redwood's principal in the customer account.

Dexter (SRE): Can we get the exact principal ARN we need to add? Also confirm whether they use cross-account IAM role or an external-id pattern. We prefer a role-based assume-role with external-id for security.

Anna (CS): I'll ask them for the role ARN and the external-id. They said they have a rotation window: 2024-11-05 02:00-04:00 UTC. They want minimal downtime.

Raj (Solutions): Minimal downtime steps I suggest: 1) Add Redwood assume-role ARN to the CMK key policy ahead of rotation 2) Ensure CloudTrail is writing to their S3 and we have read access 3) Test a read/decrypt call with the new key before cutover.

Maria (NetEng): For network: if they're using KMS via public endpoints, we need NAT/GW egress from the private subnets to KMS endpoints. Better: set up interface VPC endpoints for kms and s3 in their VPC and allow our ENIs to reach them. Also check security group egress rules.

Dexter (SRE): Note on audit logs: we recommend CloudTrail + S3 + S3 event notifications to forward to their Splunk. If they want us to push logs into their SIEM, we need a write IAM role in their account or a signed HTTP endpoint. Which did they prefer?

Anna (CS): They prefer Splunk HEC ingest. They can create an internal endpoint but asked if Redwood can push.

Raj (Solutions): Pushing is fine but requires a short-lived token and an IAM role to pull S3 objects and post. We should avoid long-lived credentials.

Maria (NetEng): One more gotcha: when CMK is rotated, key id changes but aliases stay same. Ensure our config resolves alias, not hard-coded key-id. If they rotate and we cached key-id, decryption will fail.

Dexter (SRE): Can we add an automated pre-rotation checklist to the onboarding runbook? Quick items: key policy includes Redwood role, alias used in config, test decrypt of a small envelope, S3 read list, vpc endpoints verified.

Anna (CS): I'll propose the checklist to CopperGate and schedule a 30min blackout drill during their window. Also flagging renewal risk: their trial credits end in 3 weeks and they're expecting this rotation to go smoothly before committing.

Raj (Solutions): I'll draft the policy snippet they can drop into CMK policy. Example: ```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowRedwoodAssumeRole",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REPLACEME:role/redwood-assume"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey","kms:Encrypt"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

Anna (CS): Perfect — please share that in the ticket. I'll also ask for the Splunk HEC endpoint + cert details.

kms-bot: Reminder: documented best practice for CMK rotation at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotate-keys.html :bell:

Maria (NetEng): I'll run a quick network validation script against their VPC endpoints once they provide ids. Small script we run: ```bash
nc -zv <kms-vpce-dns> 443
aws s3api head-bucket --bucket their-audit-bucket --profile crossacct
```

Dexter (SRE): OK once we get role ARN + endpoint I'll schedule a canary decrypt and an audit log fetch. If anything fails we fallback to their previous key for 24h.

Anna (CS): Thanks team. I'll update CopperGate and gather the ARNs today. Keeping this thread for the checklist and timestamps. :thumbsup:
